CAMDEN, N.J. and BRYN MAWR, Pa. , Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- American Water Works Company, Inc. (NYSE: AWK) ("American Water") and Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) ("Essential Utilities") today announced that the Illinois Commerce Commission issued an order approving the companies' proposed merger, marking the fourth favorable regulatory action toward completion of the transaction.

The companies previously received approval of the merger from the following regulatory commissions:

  • Virginia State Corporation Commission on June 22, 2026;
  • Public Utilities Commission of Ohio on May 13, 2026; and
  • Kentucky Public Service Commission on April 21, 2026.

Providing further momentum, settlement agreements in the merger approval proceedings have been reached in Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Texas, and New Jersey. Each agreement remains subject to review and approval by the applicable public utility commission.

Additionally, the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act expired on August 14, 2026, and shareholders of both companies overwhelmingly approved the transaction earlier this year.

The all-stock merger, announced October 27, 2025, will create a combined company serving more than 4.7 million water and wastewater customer connections and more than 740,000 natural gas customer connections. The combined company will operate under the American Water name and be headquartered in Camden, New Jersey.

The merger is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027, but remains subject to customary closing conditions, including, among others, required regulatory approvals, including approval from the remaining applicable public utility commissions.

For additional details regarding the transaction, please visit americanwateressentialutilitiesmerger.com.

About American Water
American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Essential Utilities
Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities. With a focus on water, wastewater, and natural gas, Essential is committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status. We are advocates for the communities we serve and are dedicated stewards of natural lands, protecting thousands of acres of forests and other habitats throughout our footprint.  Operating as the Aqua and Peoples brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across nine states. Essential is one of the most significant publicly traded water, wastewater service and natural gas providers in the U.S. Learn more at www.essential.co.

Program Services fee growth accompanied a wider quarterly net loss and lower book value per common share.

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kestrel Group Ltd (NASDAQ: KG) ("Kestrel" or the "Company") a leading specialty insurance platform that provides fronting services to program managers, reinsurers, and reinsurance brokers, today reported its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Key Highlights – Third Quarter 2026 Financials

  • Program Services fee income of $2.9 million, up 203% year over year with a 71% margin on fee revenue
  • Program Services fee revenue of $4.1 million, up 151% year over year
  • Premium produced(1) by Program Services clients was $121.2 million, up 132% year over year
  • Total revenues were $4.8 million
  • Net premiums earned were $1.9 million
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company's book value per common share(2) was $12.44
  • Net loss was $16.4 million, or a loss of $2.09 per share

Commenting on the results, Kestrel's Chief Executive Officer, Luke Ledbetter, stated, "Our Program Services segment continues to demonstrate strong sequential growth, with fee income, fee revenue and premium produced up once again, both from the second quarter of 2026 and year-over-year. This marks improvement in each quarter of 2026, driven by solid execution and our expanding pipeline of opportunity, and we are encouraged by the positive momentum within this segment. As we focus on the areas of our business with the greatest potential return for shareholders, we remain committed to optimizing our cost structure. Toward that end, we are pursuing broad-based expense reduction initiatives which have made significant progress during the third quarter, and we are targeting approximately $5 million in run-rate expense savings over the next year."

Program Services Segment

The Program Services segment provides fronting services to general agents and insurance carriers to leverage Kestrel's trusted reputation to provide access to the U.S. property and casualty insurance market and insurance paper rated "A-" (Excellent) by A.M. Best and expansive licenses in exchange for fees. Kestrel issues the policy through exclusive use of four insurance carriers, and those carriers presently retain and reinsure the risk. The Company continues to actively pursue reinsurance mechanisms with its existing partners that would selectively deploy the Company's underwriting capacity that it believes could facilitate and accelerate both its fee and premium revenue growth.

Program Services' fee income for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.9 million, up 203% compared to the same quarter in 2025. Total fee revenues for the quarter were $4.1 million, up 151% from the third quarter of 2025, driven by growth in both existing and new client accounts. Premium produced(1) by client programs totaled $121.2 million for the quarter, up 132% year over year.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Program Services' fee income was $6.9 million, compared to $1.0 million for the same period in 2025. Total fee revenues for the period were $10.9 million, compared to $3.0 million in 2025, reflecting higher premium produced by both new and existing client programs. Premium produced(1) for the nine months totaled $325.0 million, up 244% from the prior-year period.

Legacy Reinsurance Segment

The Legacy Reinsurance segment consists of the AmTrust Reinsurance and Diversified Reinsurance segments previously reported by Maiden Holdings, Ltd. ("Maiden") prior to the Combination with Kestrel. The AmTrust portion of this segment includes all business ceded to Maiden Reinsurance Ltd. by AmTrust. The Diversified portion of this segment consists of a run-off portfolio of predominantly third-party property and casualty reinsurance business focusing on regional and specialty property and casualty insurance companies located primarily in Europe, as well as business produced by Maiden LF and Maiden GF along with transactions entered into by Genesis Legacy Solutions.

During the third quarter of 2026, the Legacy Reinsurance segment reported an underwriting loss of $6.4 million, consisting of $0.1 million of underwriting income from the AmTrust business and a $6.5 million underwriting loss from the Diversified business.

The AmTrust business reported a current accident year underwriting loss of $1.4 million as the run-off of certain remaining multiple-year policies continues. This was offset by net favorable prior period development ("PPD") of $1.4 million, primarily experienced from movement not subject to the LPT/ADC Agreement including favorable movement in Workers' Compensation and Program exposure partially offset by adverse development in Specialty Risk lines of business in the AmTrust Quota Share. PPD was also affected by foreign currency movements on loss reserves denominated in non-USD currencies, which had an adverse impact of $1.3 million. Excluding foreign exchange, PPD for the AmTrust business was favorable by $2.7 million.

The Diversified business' results largely reflect the ongoing run-off of the Company's international operations. Its $6.5 million underwriting loss included $3.1 million of loss development on the German Auto quota share in the IIS unit, after the cedant triggered contractual inflation-related adjustments that increased the Company's exposure, and a $2.4 million settlement of a Genesis Legacy Solutions claim.

Investment Activities and Other Gains

The Company reported a net loss from investment activities of $1.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, consisting of net investment income of $2.3 million, offset by net realized and unrealized investment losses of $3.6 million, which reflected fair value adjustments on certain of the Company's alternative and real estate assets.

The Company also recognized foreign exchange and other gains of $0.7 million for the quarter, primarily consisting of $0.5 million of net foreign exchange gains and a $0.1 million gain from the revaluation of a contingent receivable in the insurance distribution industry. The foreign exchange gains resulted from the appreciation of the U.S. dollar on the remeasurement of net loss reserves and insurance-related liabilities denominated in non-USD currencies.

General and Administrative Expenses

Total general and administrative expenses were $11.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $11.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. Segment G&A expenses fell to $3.4 million from $4.4 million. Corporate G&A expenses rose to $8.0 million from $7.4 million. The increase was driven mainly by higher share-based compensation of $1.6 million (versus $0.2 million) and by higher recurring compensation, legal and professional fees. Lower non-recurring expenses of $0.5 million (versus $2.3 million) partly offset these increases.

Segment G&A expenses for the quarter included $0.3 million in fair value adjustments recognized in connection with the Company's May 27, 2025 combination with Maiden. Non-recurring segment G&A expense includes costs for the GLS arbitration while non-recurring corporate G&A expenses include costs for the restructuring and severance (including $0.5 million of employee separation charges incurred in the quarter) and the Combination. These costs are excluded from the Company's non-GAAP operating loss. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

The Company is carrying out broad-based initiatives to reduce its operating cost structure. It expects these actions to produce annualized run-rate savings of approximately $5 million, with the full run-rate expected within the next twelve months. Actions taken to date include:

  • significantly reducing costs associated with a broad range of professional and advisory services;
  • outsourcing a substantial portion of the Company's information technology infrastructure and support functions, completed early in the fourth quarter of 2026; and
  • streamlining certain internal functions, including related headcount reductions and the selective use of third-party service providers.

The Company continues to evaluate and implement a range of additional measures and may incur additional employee separation and other non-recurring charges as these initiatives are completed.

Balance Sheet

Total assets were $879.6 million at September 30, 2026, and shareholders' equity was $97.8 million.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company has available net operating loss ("NOL") carryforwards of $477.8 million for income tax purposes. Approximately $390.2 million of NOL carryforwards expire in various years beginning in 2029. As of September 30, 2026, approximately $87.6 million or 18.3% of the Company's NOL carryforwards have no expiry date under the relevant U.S. tax law.

Investor Presentation

The Company has posted an investor presentation on its website in connection with this earnings release. The presentation, dated November 2026, can be found at https://kestrelgroup.gcs-web.com/events-and-presentations/presentations.

Premium produced is an operating metric determined by management as a byproduct of the program services fees it earns and is paid by clients. Premium produced is equal to the premium written by an MGA or capacity provider, and management believes this measure is important in understanding the underlying production trends of its Program Services business and the fees it earns. Where the premium produced was not directly observable, the Company derived the premium produced by grossing up the known fee component using the applicable contractual fee percentage, including its arrangements with its insurance carrier partners.



(2)

Book value per common share is calculated using shareholders' equity divided by the number of common shares outstanding excluding unvested restricted and performance shares. Management uses growth in this metric as a prime measure of the value we are generating for our common shareholders, because management believes that growth in this metric ultimately results in growth in the Company's common share price. This metric is impacted by the Company's net income and external factors, such as interest rates, which can drive changes in unrealized gains or losses on our investment portfolio as well as share repurchases.

Segment G&A expenses and Corporate G&A expenses are non-GAAP measures based on specific allocations of total general and administrative expenses as presented in our unaudited Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations.

For purposes of these non-GAAP operating measures, the fee-generating business, which is included in our Program Services segment, is considered part of the underwriting and fee income operations of the Company. Management believes that this measure is important in evaluating the underwriting and fee income performance of the Company and its segments. This measure is also a useful tool to measure the profitability of the Company separately from the investment results and is also a widely used performance indicator in the insurance industry.

It also excludes on a non-recurring basis: (1) litigation costs related to the GLS Arbitration; (2) restructuring and severance costs; and (3) costs incurred due to the Combination; (4) Change in fair value of earn out consideration; and (5) Change in bargain purchase gain. The Company's management believes that the use of non-GAAP operating earnings (loss) and non-GAAP diluted operating earnings (loss) per common share enables investors and other users of the Company's financial information to analyze its performance in a manner similar to how management analyzes performance. Management also believes that these measures generally follow industry practice therefore allowing the users of financial information to compare the Company's performance with its industry peer group, and that the equity analysts and certain rating agencies which follow the Company, and the insurance industry as a whole, generally exclude these items from their analyses for the same reasons. Non-GAAP operating earnings should not be viewed as a substitute for U.S. GAAP net income.



(6)

Non-GAAP operating return on average shareholders' equity is a non-GAAP financial measure. Management uses non-GAAP operating return on average shareholders' equity as a measure of profitability that focuses on the return to common shareholders. SHANGHAI, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- U Power Limited (Nasdaq: UCAR) (the "Company" or "U Power"), a provider of electric vehicle (EV) battery-swapping solutions based on its proprietary UOTTA™ technology, expanding into AI-integrated energy management for transportation systems and energy infrastructure, today announced its interim unaudited financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 ("H1 2026").[1]

H1 2026 Financial Snapshot

  • Total net revenues were RMB14.8 million (US$2.2 million), a decrease of 16.5% compared with RMB17.7 million in the six months ended June 30, 2025 ("H1 2025").
  • Combined net revenues from battery-swapping services, including two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping services, increased 30.2% to RMB1.3 million (US$0.2 million), compared with RMB1.0 million in H1 2025.
  • Gross profit was RMB3.6 million (US$0.5 million), compared with RMB8.4 million in H1 2025. Gross margin was 24.5%.
  • Net loss was RMB97.6 million (US$14.4 million), compared with RMB27.4 million in H1 2025.
  • Cash and cash equivalents were RMB54.9 million (US$8.1 million) as of June 30, 2026, compared with RMB22.0 million as of December 31, 2025. Working capital was RMB123.3 million (US$18.2 million), compared with RMB65.5 million as of December 31, 2025.

Mr. Jia Li, CEO and Chairman of the Board of Directors of U Power, commented, "In the first half of 2026, we moved our two key battery-swapping projects from planning into execution. In Thailand, our first 30 battery-swapping heavy-duty trucks completed production and testing. In Hong Kong SAR, we commenced foundation works for our first MAXUS MIFA 7 battery-swapping taxi station. Subsequently, in August 2026, the first batch of these vehicles received type approval from the Transport Department, clearing them for sale in Hong Kong SAR.

"Total net revenues declined 16.5% year over year to RMB14.8 million, primarily due to the absence of sourcing services revenue, compared with RMB2.8 million in the first half of 2025, as the Thailand trucks we procured were not delivered to customers until July; and, to a lesser extent, a 3.1% decrease in revenue from sales of battery-swapping stations to RMB13.5 million. Revenue from battery-swapping services increased 30.2% year over year to RMB1.3 million as our two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping business continued to scale.

"We received RMB207.2 million from the issuance of ordinary shares in the first half and ended the period with cash and cash equivalents of RMB54.9 million and working capital of RMB123.3 million. Our net loss primarily reflected expenses related to our overseas expansion and evaluation of potential investment targets, as well as a provision for expected credit losses and higher interest expenses.

"Our focus for the second half of the year is on converting our project pipeline into deliveries and recurring revenue, including our battery-swapping heavy-duty truck project in Thailand and our battery-swapping taxi project in Hong Kong SAR. Beyond mobility, we are developing AI-driven energy management solutions for intelligent data centers through our joint venture, which we believe can open a new avenue of growth by leveraging our expertise in energy infrastructure. We remain focused on disciplined execution as we work to build U Power into a diversified sustainable mobility and energy solutions provider and create long-term value for our shareholders."

[1] All amounts presented in U.S. dollars (US$) in this news release are based on a conversion rate of RMB6.7851 to US$1.00 for the reporting period ended June 30, 2026 and are provided solely for the convenience of the reader.

H1 2026 Financial Review

Total net revenues were RMB14.8 million (US$2.2 million), a decrease of 16.5% compared with RMB17.7 million in H1 2025, primarily due to the absence of sourcing services revenue, which was RMB2.8 million in H1 2025 and accounted for 15.9% of total net revenues in H1 2025, and, to a lesser extent, lower revenue from sales of battery-swapping stations. No sourcing services revenue was recorded in H1 2026 because the vehicles the Company procured during the period had not yet been sold as of June 30, 2026.

  • Net revenues from sales of battery-swapping stations were RMB13.5 million (US$2.0 million), a decrease of 3.1% compared with RMB13.9 million in H1 2025, and accounted for 91.0% of total net revenues.
  • Combined net revenues from battery-swapping services, including two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping services, were RMB1.3 million (US$0.2 million), an increase of 30.2% compared with RMB1.0 million in H1 2025, and accounted for 9.0% of total net revenues. Revenues from two-wheeled vehicle battery-swapping services increased to RMB1.286 million from RMB0.675 million in H1 2025, partially offset by a decrease in revenues from other battery-swapping services to RMB0.039 million from RMB0.343 million in H1 2025.

Gross profit was RMB3.6 million (US$0.5 million), a decrease of 56.8% from RMB8.4 million in H1 2025, primarily due to lower gross profit from product sales, which fell to RMB4.2 million from RMB7.6 million in H1 2025. The decline primarily reflected the absence of sales of high-gross-margin battery-swapping stations by U SWAP, the Company's subsidiary in Thailand, which had occurred in H1 2025, as well as the sale of three additional battery-swapping stations with lower gross margins in H1 2026. Gross margin was 24.5%, compared with 47.3% in H1 2025, primarily due to the aforementioned factors along with higher per-unit procurement costs for the stations sold.

Total operating expenses were RMB83.8 million (US$12.3 million), an increase of 224.1% from RMB25.9 million in H1 2025, primarily reflecting higher general and administrative expenses and a provision for expected credit losses of RMB15.2 million (US$2.2 million), compared with a reversal of RMB3.9 million in H1 2025.

  • General and administrative expenses were RMB64.2 million (US$9.5 million), an increase of 161.5% from RMB24.6 million in H1 2025, primarily due to expenditures of approximately RMB11.7 million in identifying potential investment targets, approximately RMB11.2 million of consulting and other fees related to the localization of the Company's business in Thailand, approximately RMB5.1 million of operating and maintenance costs attributable to the Company's new business, and operating and maintenance costs incurred by newly added subsidiaries.
  • Research and development expenses were RMB3.3 million (US$0.5 million), a decrease of 4.4% from RMB3.4 million in H1 2025.
  • Sales and marketing expenses were RMB1.1 million (US$0.2 million), a decrease of 39.5% from RMB1.8 million in H1 2025, primarily attributable to reduced overseas business activities.

Interest income was RMB1.4 million (US$0.2 million), compared with RMB0.02 million in H1 2025, primarily due to higher interest income from third-party loans. Interest expenses were RMB9.0 million (US$1.3 million), compared with RMB0.2 million in H1 2025, primarily due to increases in loan interest and bank charges.

Net loss was RMB97.6 million (US$14.4 million), compared with a net loss of RMB27.4 million in H1 2025, primarily attributable to expenses related to overseas expansion and evaluation of potential investment targets, as well as a provision for expected credit losses and higher interest expenses. Net loss attributable to the Company's shareholders was RMB75.5 million (US$11.1 million), compared with RMB22.0 million in H1 2025.

Basic and diluted losses per ordinary share were RMB150.11 (US$22.13), compared with RMB1,157.27 in H1 2025, with weighted average ordinary shares outstanding of 502,968 and 19,010, respectively; per-share amounts for both periods have been retrospectively restated for the April 2026 share consolidation (1-for-10, effective April 1, 2026) and the September 2026 share consolidation (1-for-20, effective September 9, 2026).

Cash and cash equivalents were RMB54.9 million (US$8.1 million) as of June 30, 2026, compared with RMB22.0 million as of December 31, 2025, and working capital was RMB123.3 million (US$18.2 million), compared with RMB65.5 million. Total assets were RMB501.6 million (US$73.9 million), total liabilities were RMB104.8 million (US$15.4 million), and total shareholders' equity attributable to the Company's shareholders was RMB401.2 million (US$59.1 million), compared with RMB378.8 million, RMB84.2 million and RMB271.0 million, respectively, as of December 31, 2025.

Year-to-Date 2026 Operational Milestones

  • Thailand: Completed comprehensive operational testing and full-stack integration of the battery-swapping system on heavy-duty truck prototypes and completed production of the first batch of 30 trucks for Whale Logistics (Thailand) Co., Ltd., under a strategic partnership signed in December 2025 for the deployment of up to 1,000 battery-swapping electric truck tractors. The first batch arrived in Thailand in June 2026 and was delivered in July 2026. Construction of the first supporting battery-swapping station is under way, and the Company expects to complete its delivery in the second half of 2026.
  • Hong Kong SAR: In the first half of 2026, the Company commenced foundation works for the first MAXUS MIFA 7 battery-swapping taxi station at Container Terminal 9, Tsing Yi. The first batch of these vehicles to arrive in Hong Kong SAR received type approval from the Transport Department in August, clearing them for sale in Hong Kong SAR. The Company has been promoting the MIFA 7 battery-swapping taxi and the related battery-swapping operating model to taxi operators in Hong Kong SAR, and has received positive feedback from the industry. The Company expects to commence trial operation of battery-swapping services in Hong Kong SAR and start delivering battery-swap MIFA 7 vehicles to taxi companies by the end of 2026.
  • AI-driven intelligent data center (IDC) energy solutions: In April 2026, formed a joint venture with Guofu Hydrogen Energy (Hong Kong) Development Co., Limited (HKSE: 2582) and Cloud Digital Chain Limited to provide AI-driven energy management for IDCs, marking U Power's strategic expansion into the energy management solutions sector. In May 2026, the joint venture entered into an agreement with CEWA Group and Jiangsu Guofu Hydrogen Energy Equipment Co., Ltd. to develop an integrated energy solution for a planned 100MW data center in Rayong, Thailand, beginning with a 3MW pilot project.
  • Private placement: In August 2026, after the end of the reporting period, the Company completed a US$16 million private placement of 9,756,100 Class A ordinary shares to four existing shareholders at US$1.64 per share, equivalent to approximately 487,805 Class A ordinary shares at approximately US$32.80 per share after giving effect to the September 2026 share consolidation.

About U Power Limited

U Power is a provider of electric vehicle (EV) battery-swapping solutions based on its proprietary UOTTA™ technology, expanding into AI-integrated energy management for transportation systems and energy infrastructure. The Company has built a scalable network supporting commercial EV operations across multiple international markets.

U Power is now evolving beyond battery-swapping into an AI-driven, multi-energy ecosystem spanning EV infrastructure, smart energy management, and hydrogen power generation. Through a joint venture with a hydrogen technology company, the Company is developing integrated hydrogen-electric solutions for an Artificial Intelligence Data Center (AIDC) and EV charging and battery-swapping infrastructure, providing power support for electric mobility and the global AIDC industry.

For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://www.upower-limited.com/.

Each Board believes each Fund’s distribution policy maintains a stable, high rate of distribution. These distributions are not tied to each Fund’s investment income or capital gains and do not represent yield or investment return on each Fund’s portfolio. The Distribution Amount from one calendar year to the next will increase or decrease based on the change in each Fund’s net asset value. The terms of each distribution policy are reviewed and approved at least annually by each Fund’s Board and may be modified at their discretion for the benefit of each Fund and its stockholders.

Each Fund’s Board remains convinced its stockholders are well served by a policy of regular distributions which increase liquidity and provide flexibility to individual stockholders in managing their investment in each Fund. Stockholders have the option of reinvesting these distributions in additional shares of their Fund or receiving them in cash. Stockholders may consider reinvesting their regular distributions through their Fund’s dividend reinvestment plan, which may at times provide additional benefit to stockholders who participate in their Fund’s plan. Under each Fund’s distribution policy, each Fund may distribute to stockholders each month a minimum fixed percentage per year of the net asset value or market price per share of its common stock or at least a minimum fixed dollar amount per year. In determining to adopt this policy, the Board of each Fund sought to make regular monthly distributions throughout the year. Under each policy, each Fund’s distributions will consist either of (1) earnings, (2) capital gains, or (3) return-of-capital, or some combination of one or more of these categories. A return-of-capital is the return of a portion of the stockholder’s original investment.

Given the current economic environment and the composition of each Fund’s portfolio, a portion of each Fund’s distributions made during the current calendar year is expected to consist of a return of the stockholder’s capital. Accordingly, these distributions should not be confused with yield or investment return on each Fund’s portfolio. The final composition of the distributions for 2026 cannot be determined until after the end of the year and is subject to change depending on market conditions during the year and the magnitude of income and realized gains for the year.

In any given year, there can be no guarantee each Fund’s investment returns will exceed the amount of the net distributions. To the extent the amount of distributions paid to stockholders in cash exceeds the total net investment returns of the Fund, the assets of a Fund will decline. If the total net investment returns exceed the amount of cash distributions, the assets of a Fund will increase. Distributions designated as return-of-capital are not taxed as ordinary income dividends and are referred to as tax-free dividends or nontaxable distributions. A return-of-capital distribution reduces the cost basis of a stockholder’s shares in the Fund. Stockholders can expect to receive tax-reporting information for 2026 distributions by the middle of February 2027, indicating the exact composition per share of the distributions received during the calendar year. WEST PALM BEACH, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Domestic Supply Chains Remain a Strategic Theme

The expansion of electric transportation and battery-based energy storage has kept lithium in focus across the global materials market. At the same time, manufacturers and policymakers continue to examine supply-chain resilience and the potential contribution of North American sources.

Against this backdrop, ELEKTROS Inc. (OTC PINK:ELEK), a publicly traded company on the OTC market, is evaluating a potential hard-rock lithium property in northern New York, close to the Canadian border but located on the U.S. side. The review is preliminary and exploratory. The company has not completed or announced an acquisition, verified a mineral resource or reserve independently, or established the economic viability of the property.

Potential Benefits of a U.S. Location

Should geological work and subsequent diligence support the opportunity, a domestic project could potentially create access to U.S. processing pathways and customers. Depending on the location, infrastructure and ultimate commercial arrangements, domestic sourcing could also reduce the need for some overseas shipping and international import-related steps.

These possibilities remain conditional. ELEKTROS has not established that the property contains an economically recoverable lithium deposit, that required permits can be obtained, or that a project would generate commercial returns.

Industry Outlook Highlights the Scale of the Market

An October 22, 2026 Benzinga article, "Lithium's $100 Billion Supply Gap Hands Albemarle a Domestic Moat," cited Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projections that worldwide lithium demand could more than triple by 2050. The cited outlook suggested that meeting potential demand could require 134 additional mines and investment exceeding $100 billion, reflecting growth in electric vehicles and stationary storage.

The industry outlook is not an ELEKTROS forecast and should not be interpreted as evidence of a resource, valuation or future performance for the New York property. The cited article focused on companies other than ELEKTROS.

Separate Workstreams: Lithium and EV Charging

In parallel with its lithium-related evaluation, ELEKTROS continues to explore possible development relationships associated with its multi-port EV charging patent, U.S. Patent No. 12,522,100 B1. The company considers the lithium opportunity and EV charging technology separate initiatives within its broader areas of interest.

No prototype launch, licensing transaction, commercial deployment, customer adoption or patent-derived revenue is being reported at this time.

A Disciplined Review Before Any Decision

The company's evaluation may include verification of property and mineral rights, independent geological assessment and sampling, review of environmental and land-use obligations, permitting analysis, potential processing and transportation routes, financing considerations and possible transaction terms.

ELEKTROS recognizes that a promising concept must be tested against technical evidence and realistic economics. The company will consider the findings and associated risks before deciding whether any further step is appropriate.

Shareholder Perspective

ELEKTROS appreciates the attention of shareholders and market participants interested in the future of domestic lithium supply. Management intends to pursue its evaluation with determination while maintaining a clear distinction between an opportunity under review and a project that has been proven, permitted or placed into production.

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Faraday Future Intelligent Electric Inc. (NASDAQ: FFAI) (“Faraday Future,” “FF” or the “Company”), a California-based global Embodied AI (EAI) ecosystem company, today announced that it plans to hold a Special Meeting of Stockholders (the “Special Meeting”) on December 15, 2026, subject to confirmation, to seek approval of a Reverse Stock Split Proposal and an Adjournment Proposal.

Faraday Future Plans to Hold a Special Meeting of Stockholders on December 15 to Seek Approval of Key Proposals

The Reverse Stock Split Proposal would provide the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) with additional flexibility to manage the Company’s capital structure and support the Company’s efforts to maintain compliance with Nasdaq’s continued listing requirements.

The Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”) urges all stockholders to vote FOR all proposals.

Proposal Highlights:

Reverse Stock Split Proposal

The Company is seeking stockholder approval of a reverse stock split of its Class A and Class B common stock at a ratio of up to 1-for-80. If approved, the Board would have discretion to determine the final ratio and timing of any reverse stock split within one year following the Special Meeting.

Stockholder approval would not by itself mean that a reverse stock split will be implemented. The Board would evaluate market conditions and the best interests of the Company and its stockholders in determining whether and when to implement a reverse stock split within the approved parameters.

Adjournment Proposal

The Company is also seeking stockholder approval to adjourn the Special Meeting one or more times, if necessary or appropriate, including to allow additional time for the solicitation of proxies.

Additional details regarding the proposals to be voted on at the Special Meeting, including their background, rationale and voting procedures, can be found in the preliminary proxy statement, which the Company filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) on November 6, 2026. A reverse stock split reduces a company's number of outstanding shares while raising the price per share proportionally, so the total value of each investor's holding is unchanged; a 1-for-10 split turns 100 shares worth $1 each into 10 shares worth $10 each. Companies often do this to regain compliance with an exchange's minimum price rule or to attract investors who avoid very low-priced stocks.
proxy statementregulatory
A proxy statement is a document companies send to shareholders ahead of a meeting that lays out the items up for a vote—like who will sit on the board, executive pay, and major corporate decisions—and provides background so shareholders can decide how to cast their votes or appoint someone to vote for them. Think of it as an agenda plus a ballot and briefing notes, important because the outcomes can change control, strategy, and value.

PHILADELPHIA, PA / ACCESS Newswire / November 6, 2026 / Medicus Pharma Ltd. (NASDAQ:MDCX) ("Medicus" or the "Company"), a precision guided, biotech/life sciences company focused on advancing the clinical development programs of novel and potentially disruptive therapeutic assets, today reported financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update highlighting capital efficient strategic, clinical and regulatory progress across its development portfolio.

During the third quarter of 2026, Medicus entered into a co-development and license agreement with Pfizer Inc. ("Pfizer") for PF-08046031 (CD228V), a clinical-stage antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) targeting melanotransferrin, or CD228. The Company subsequently designated CD228V as its principal development priority, with an initial focus on establishing clinical proof-of-concept in melanoma.

During and after the quarter, the Company achieved several important milestones, including the announcement of an exclusive development focus for SkinJect® in Gorlin syndrome and the submission of an optimized Teverelix® registrational protocol to the FDA for advanced prostate cancer. On November 4, 2026, Medicus announced a non-binding LOI (as defined below) for a proposed Business Combination (as defined below) between SkinJect and an undisclosed special purpose acquisition company. In addition, following the Share Consolidation (as defined below), the Company regained compliance with Nasdaq's minimum bid price requirement.

During the quarter and on an ongoing basis, the Company has highlighted a capital-efficient portfolio strategy, which combines focused development of CD228V with essential support for SkinJect® and Teverelix® as partner-ready therapeutic programs. The Company is allocating resources to maintain these programs and keep their development packages current while pursuing the proposed SkinJect Business Combination and strategic partnerships for Teverelix®.

Management Commentary

"The third quarter saw the transformation of Medicus into a precision oncology-led biotech company with CD228V as our principal development priority," stated Dr. Raza Bokhari, Medicus Executive Chairman and CEO. "With capital-efficient allocation of resources, we remain focused on disciplined execution, regulatory excellence and strategic growth as we seek to build long-term shareholder value and advance therapies with the potential to improve patient outcomes."

Financial Highlights (Q3 2026)

As disclosed in the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, financial results include:

  • Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash: $13.1 million.
  • Cash and cash equivalents: $5.0 million (vs.$8.7 million as of December 31, 2025).
  • Total Operating expenses (loss from operations): $14.5 million (vs. $15.4 million in Q3 2025).
  • General and administrative expenses: $2.5 million (vs. $5.0 million in Q3 2025).
  • Research and development expenses: $2.0 million (vs. $1.7 million in Q3 2025).
  • Net loss: $15.2 million (vs. $16.0 million in Q3 2025).
  • Net loss per share*: $11.64 (vs. $56.18 in Q3 2025).

* Share and per share amounts for all periods have been retroactively adjusted to reflect the Company's 50-to-1 share consolidation effective October 12, 2026 (the "Share Consolidation").

The Company's complete unaudited financial statements and results of operations for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, are included in its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 6, 2026 (the "Form 10-Q").

Third Quarter 2026 and Subsequent Operational Highlights

During and after the third quarter, Medicus established its revised portfolio priorities. The following summarizes the key developments and current program status.

CD228V License and Co-Development:

  • Worldwide license. On September 2, 2026, the Company through its wholly owned subsidiary, Medicus Pharma Inc., entered into a co-development and licensing agreement with Pfizer providing an exclusive worldwide license to develop, manufacture and commercialize CD228V, subject to Pfizer's retained rights and other contractual provisions. Under the agreement, the Company controls program execution under the co-development framework.
  • Clinical development focus. CD228V is a second-generation CD228-targeted ADC, utilizing Pfizer's established vedotin linker-payload platform. Medicus intends to pursue initial proof-of-concept in relapsed, refractory or immunotherapy-resistant melanoma, supported by the existing U.S. investigational new drug application (IND) for CD228V and a first-in-human Phase 1 clinical study.
  • Pfizer participation. Pfizer provided $2.0 million in development funding and retains the right, without an obligation, to elect to fund all or part of development beginning with the first pivotal trial, subject to a further definitive agreement in respect of such arrangements.

SkinJect Proposed Business Combination and Gorlin Syndrome Development

On November 4, 2026, Medicus announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, SkinJect®, Inc. ("SkinJect"), had entered a non-binding letter of intent ("LOI") with an undisclosed special purpose acquisition company ("SPAC") for a proposed business combination involving SkinJect®(the "Business Combination").

  • Proposed valuation and financing. The LOI contemplates an approximate $135 million pre-money enterprise valuation for SkinJect as well as a concurrent equity financing at closing of the proposed Business Transaction to support the SKNJCT-005 study in Gorlin syndrome and preparation and submission of a potential New Drug Application ("NDA"). Clinical package and indication focus. In September, the Company announced an exclusive development focus on evaluating SkinJect® in treating multiple basal cell carcinoma lesions in patients with Gorlin syndrome and concluded any further development in sporadic nodular BCC. The clinical study report for the completed SKNJCT-003 Phase 2 study was finalized that month, and, among other things, the Company believes that it provides a basis for potential partners to assess the next development program.
  • Study authorization. In July, the FDA issued a "Study May Proceed" letter for SKNJCT-005, the planned registrational Phase 2b study in Gorlin syndrome. The authorization permits initiation of the study under the existing IND. SkinJect® remains investigational, and any NDA submission or approval would depend on clinical results and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Designation applications. The FDA has held review of the Company's Orphan Drug Designation and Rare Pediatric Disease Designation applications in abeyance pending receipt of additional information from the Company.

Teverelix® Partner Ready Therapeutic Programs

The Company views Teverelix® as a portfolio of partner-ready opportunities in urology, advanced prostate cancer and women's health. Existing clinical work, regulatory engagement and proposed study designs provide defined programs for potential partners to evaluate. Medicus is allocating essential resources to maintain program readiness and keep development documentation current as it seeks partners with the capabilities and resources to advance these opportunities.

  • Advanced prostate cancer. On September 29, 2026, Medicus announced that it had submitted to the FDA a proposed seamless Phase 2b/3 registration-intent protocol for Teverelix® for patients at increased cardiovascular risk. The design is expected to begin with approximately 80 randomized patients and, if predefined continuation criteria are met, enroll approximately 528 additional patients, for a total of approximately 608 patients. The proposal remains subject to FDA feedback and there can be no assurance that the FDA will agree with the proposed protocol. Medicus intends to seek an out-license or other strategic partnership rather than independently fund the proposed study; however, there can be no assurance that the Company will successfully enter into any such transaction.

Other Corporate Developments:

During and after the quarter, Medicus also advanced initiatives, aimed at fostering long-term growth and building shareholder value. Medicus and YA II PN, Ltd. ("Yorkville") mutually agreed to terminate the standby equity purchase agreement (the "SEPA") effective September 11, 2026. No borrowings, advance notices or shares to be issued remained outstanding under the SEPA at the time of its termination.

Following the Share Consolidation, Medicus announced on October 26, 2026, that it had received written notice from Nasdaq on October 23, 2026, confirming that the Company had regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement.

Anticipated Clinical Development and Partnering Priorities

The Company intends to focus in the coming quarters on capital-efficiency and disciplined execution. Medicus is focused on concentrating incremental development investment on selected CD228V milestones. Essential resources will continue to support current clinical and regulatory documentation, manufacturing information and readiness activities as the Company pursues the proposed SkinJect® Business Combination, including definitive agreements and concurrent financing, and strategic partnerships for Teverelix®. There can be no assurance that definitive agreements will be signed, that the financing will be secured or that the Business Combination will be completed on favorable terms or at all.

"This report highlights the progress we have made and our ongoing efforts to continue creating long-term value for our shareholders, customers, employees, and the communities we serve." 

AZZ's commitment to responsible business practices continues to gain national recognition. In 2026, Newsweek named AZZ one of America's Most Responsible Companies for the fourth consecutive year. Additionally, USA Today named the Company as one of America's 2026 Climate Leaders. This recognition reflects the collective efforts of AZZ's employees and reinforces the Company's commitment to operating our business responsibly, ethically, and sustainably.

This is AZZ's sixth consecutive annual sustainability report, available to view and download on the Company's website at www.azz.com/sustainability.

"Together, we will continue building on the legacy established in 1956, honoring the contributions of those who came before us, while creating new opportunities for future generations of AZZ employees, their families, and the communities where we live and work," concluded Ferguson.

AZZ Inc. is the leading independent provider of hot-dip galvanizing and coil coating solutions to a broad range of end-markets. Collectively, our business segments provide sustainable, unmatched metal coating solutions that enhance the longevity and appearance of buildings, products and infrastructure that are essential to everyday life.

Bloom's contribution to the Firefighter Community Fund will support families facing food insecurity across Oxford and Lafayette County

SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) continued its season-long partnership with ESPN Radio's College Football Campus Tour this week in Oxford, Mississippi, ahead of Saturday's Georgia-Ole Miss matchup.

Ahead of the game, Bloom visited Oxford Fire Department Station 1 at 399 McElroy Drive and presented a $10,000 donation to the Firefighter Community Fund, a nonprofit established by members of the Oxford Fire Department to support local families facing food insecurity.

The Firefighter Community Fund works with Oxford Love Packs and Commodores Care to provide financial assistance and essential goods to children and families across Oxford and Lafayette County. The organization also provides Thanksgiving meals to families in need, with its work funded through community donations and events including the annual 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb.

“The strongest communities are built by people who look out for one another, often in ways most of us never see,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “Oxford’s firefighters do more than respond when their neighbors need help. Through the Firefighter Community Fund, they are addressing needs in their community long before an emergency call comes in. We are proud to support that commitment and the families it reaches across Oxford and Lafayette County.”

“Our firefighters see firsthand the needs families in our community face, and being there for our community is at the heart of what we do,” said Josh Ferguson, Director of the Firefighter Community Fund. “We’re grateful for Bloom Energy’s support, which will help us reach and feed more local families at a time of year when coming together and looking out for our neighbors means so much.”

The Oxford visit is part of Bloom's season-long partnership with ESPN Radio's College Football Campus Tour, which is bringing Bloom to college communities across the country and using each stop to recognize the firefighters and first responders who help keep those communities safe.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Georgia-Ole Miss game as ESPN Radio's College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Oxford.
